chunks: And with this chain of transmission:
Concerning a slave who put out the eye of a free man, while the slave had a debt upon him, he said:
Let his eye be put out, and let the debt of the creditors be nullified.

key_terms.الْغُرَمَاءِ: the creditors; those owed repayment of the debt
key_terms.حُرٍّ: a free person; the victim in the case
key_terms.دَيْنٌ: debt; a financial liability owed by the slave
key_terms.عَبْدٍ: a slave; the offender in this legal case
key_terms.عَيْنَ: the eye; the injured organ subject to qisas
key_terms.فَقَأَ: put out or gouged; referring to the destruction of the eye
key_terms.لِتُفْقَأْ: let it be put out; an instruction to carry out retaliatory punishment
key_terms.يَبْطُلَ: be nullified or become void; referring to the creditors' debt claims

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if an indebted slave puts out the eye of a free man?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding qisas in a case where a slave injures a free man by putting out his eye while the slave is indebted. It indicates that qisas is carried out on the offending slave, and the claims of the creditors are thereby invalidated in relation to him.
